correctness.rationale: Fixed-point equality is enough to reconstruct the law. Because X^e has a Lebesgue density, a fixed X is absolutely continuous. With a=E|X|, density equality gives F'=F/a a.e. on (-infinity,0) and F'=(1-F)/a a.e. on (0,infinity). Integrating factors yield F(x)=p e^{x/a} on the negative side and 1-F(x)=(1-p)e^{-x/a} on the positive side; absolute continuity removes a zero atom and enforces the common boundary mass. Conversely the displayed signed-exponential law has E|X|=a and substitution reproduces the same density. Endpoints p=0,1 and p=1/2 are correctly handled.
risks: No claim is made about iterates, attraction, rates, or nontrivial cycles.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete fixed-point classification for a recently introduced probability transform. It identifies the precise structural freedom created by two-sided support: exponential memorylessness remains in magnitude while an arbitrary independent sign bias survives. Complete fixed-point sets are useful baselines for transform iteration and approximation theory, so the result is more than a cosmetic ODE exercise.
risks: Its main value is structural classification rather than a quantitative convergence theorem.

limitations: Only the exact transform in the cited 2025 definition is classified.
No statement about iterative attraction, rates, or cycles is made.
